content.title: About
content.content: Cafe Mocha is a fragrant beverage made from espresso, steamed milk, and chocolate syrup, often topped with whipped cream. It blends the robustness of coffee with the sweetness of chocolate, creating a rich, velvety flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “mocha” comes from the Yemeni port of Mocha, historically known for its aromatic coffee beans.
The first mocha recipe appeared in the early 1920s in the United States when baristas began adding chocolate syrup to coffee.
Mocha is commonly served in tall glasses to highlight its layered appearance.
A cold version, iced mocha, is popular during warm weather.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Both coffee and dark chocolate are rich in polyphenols, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Caffeine in espresso stimulates the central nervous system, improving alertness and concentration.

items.title: Mood enhancement
items.content: The combination of caffeine and theobromine from chocolate may contribute to a better mood.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Mocha provides magnesium and potassium, essential for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: Caffeine can increase metabolic rate, potentially aiding calorie burning.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: High caffeine intake may cause anxiety, insomnia, and rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Chocolate syrup adds significant sugar, which can be problematic for diabetics or those watching weight.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Coffee can exacerbate gastritis and heartburn in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy should use dairy‑free alternatives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve cafe mocha hot, typically in a 240–350 ml cup, topped with whipped cream. Variations may include vanilla or caramel syrups. For a lighter version, use skim milk or plant‑based milks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store syrup and milk in the refrigerator, and keep ground coffee in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from light. Prepared drinks should be consumed within 2–3 hours.
